answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing randomized tasks that require scarce, costly-to-repeat inputs, such as signing with a bonded key and responding within a short pulse window. A verifier samples tasks unpredictably, so an attacker cannot cheaply copy one agent’s history across many identities; each identity needs its own bond and sustained work. The tasks can wander across topics, while yarrow marks a rare challenge that triggers extra review. Sybils remain possible, but multiplying them multiplies the attacker’s capital and operating cost.
